item: Is damages for non-performance due only after the debtor has been put on notice (general rule of the Civil Code on compensation, around article 179), and is there a contrary text for the matter at hand?
In a bilateral contract, must the creditor serve a formal notice before asking the court for performance or rescission (around article 119), and are damages available in either case?
Is a formal notice required before asking for performance in kind (around article 164, referring to the articles on notice)?
What form must the formal notice take: a warning (إنذار) or an act that stands in its place (around article 180)?
May the formal notice be sent by post, and in what way does the Civil Code allow this (around article 180)?
May the parties agree that the debtor is in default by the mere arrival of the due date, without any step (around article 180)?
Does a bailiff (محضر قضائي) serve the formal notice, and which text gives the bailiff that power (law on the bailiff profession)?
Does a registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt count as a formal notice, and does a mere letter, e-mail or phone call count?
Exemption: performance has become impossible or useless through the debtor's act (around article 181).
Exemption: the obligation is compensation for a harmful act (tort) (around article 181).
Exemption: the obligation is to return a thing the debtor knows was stolen, or a thing received without right knowingly (around article 181).
Exemption: the debtor has declared in writing that he will not perform (around article 181).
Does an express clause of automatic rescission (rescission without a court) dispense with the formal notice, or must the clause say so expressly (around article 120)?
Rescission by law when performance becomes impossible (around article 121): is a notice needed there?
Does a penalty clause (agreed damages) become due only after notice (around articles 183 to 185)?
Damages for delay in paying a sum of money (around article 186): from what moment do they run, from the notice or from the claim?
Penalty payment (غرامة تهديدية) (around articles 174 and 175): is a notice a precondition?
What is the effect of the absence of a formal notice: is the claim for damages inadmissible, rejected on the merits, or only the damages for the period before the claim lost?
Can the statement of claim itself count as the formal notice (the act that stands in the place of a warning)?
Does the court raise the lack of formal notice of its own motion, or only on the defendant's plea?
Who bears the proof of the formal notice (the creditor), and what document proves it (the bailiff's record, the acknowledgement of receipt)?
From which date does the formal notice produce effects: the date it was served or received?
Does the formal notice transfer the risk of loss of the thing to the debtor (around the articles on delivery and loss of the thing)?
Does a formal notice interrupt limitation? (That belongs to the periods module; a mere notice is usually not an interrupting act.)
Leases: is a formal notice needed before claiming unpaid rent or eviction for non-payment, and does the lease chapter have its own rule?
Commercial leases: notice to quit (التنبيه بالإخلاء) is a different act from a formal notice (belongs to commercial-lease-regimes).
Sale: is a formal notice needed before rescission for non-payment of the price, and does the sale chapter have a special rule?
Contract for works (مقاولة): notice before rescission or damages for delay or defects?
Family maintenance, wages, and tort claims: is a formal notice irrelevant there (no contract, or a contrary text)?
Administrative disputes: a prior administrative grievance (تظلم) is a different step from the civil formal notice (belongs to ordinary-court-exits).

Order to pay (أمر بالأداء): does the Code of Civil and Administrative Procedure require a prior formal notice to pay before the petition (belongs to ordinary-court-exits, but the formal notice may be the same act)?
Labour: the conciliation before the labour office is not a formal notice (belongs to labour-prelitigation).
Is there a time limit between the formal notice and the claim (a reasonable delay granted to the debtor), or may the claim be filed right after the notice?
Does the judge keep a power to grant the debtor a delay even after notice (around article 119 second paragraph, and the article on grace periods)?
Facts to state in the petition: the contract, the due date, the non-performance, the date and means of the notice, the debtor's failure after notice.
Documents to attach: the contract, the bailiff's record of the notice or the registered letter with its acknowledgement of receipt.
Amendments: Civil Code amended by law 05-10 of 2005 (articles on notice and post may have been touched); check the current wording.
Is the claim one for which a formal notice (الإعذار) is a precondition of damages for delay, or of the claim itself?
Was a formal notice actually sent to the defendant before filing, and is there proof of it?
On what date was the notice served, and did the defendant receive it (acknowledgement of receipt)?
By what means was it sent: bailiff, registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt, or another means; which means does the law accept?
Does the notice clearly call on the debtor to perform, and does it fix a reasonable period to comply?
Is the notice addressed to the right person, at the right address, and in the right capacity (debtor, heir, representative)?
Does the contract itself state that the debtor is in default by the mere passing of the term, without notice?
Is the obligation one with a fixed term, so that default arises by the term itself?
Is the notice unnecessary because performance has become impossible or useless through the debtor's act?
Is the notice unnecessary because the debtor has declared in writing that he will not perform?
Is the notice unnecessary for a debt of money arising from a wrongful act, or for restitution of something taken without right?
Is the notice unnecessary for a debt of something received without right, with bad faith of the recipient?
Is the notice unnecessary in a case where the law itself provides that default is automatic?
What is the effect of the absence of a notice: inadmissibility of the claim, or only refusal of damages for delay?
From what date do damages for delay and legal interest run: from the notice, from the filing, or from the term?
Does the claim itself (the filing of the petition) stand in place of a notice for any request?
In commercial matters, is a notice needed, and does the form differ?
Does a notice to quit or a notice to pay in a lease follow a separate regime (see the commercial lease module)?
Can the notice be replaced by a conciliation step or a prior formal summons required for the particular claim?
Does the notice interrupt a limitation period or only place the debtor in default?
Is a notice needed before rescission of a contract for non-performance, and may the judge grant a period of grace?
Can the lawyer keep a copy of the notice and of the receipt in the file as documents to annex to the petition?
Is the notice valid if sent by a means not accepted by law, and can the court still treat it as notice?
Must the notice be in Arabic, and signed by whom?
Is a fresh notice needed when the amount or the obligation changed after the first notice?
In joint or indivisible obligations, to whom must the notice go?
Is a notice needed against a public body, and does a different prior step apply?
What must the petition say about the notice (date, means, result) so that the court can check it?
